                                           NATURE OF ACTION
24         1.        This action arises from Apple Inc.’s (“Apple”) termination of Plaintiff Ex-Human
25   Inc.’s (“Ex-Human”) developer account and its concurrent decision to withhold substantial earned
26
     revenue, following allegations of “dishonest or fraudulent activity” that Apple has never explained
27
     with any specificity. Ex-Human seeks injunctive relief to restore access to the iOS platform and to
28
                                                   1
                                               COMPLAINT
       Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD           Document 1        Filed 03/31/26      Page 2 of 26



 1   recover approximately $500,000 in revenue generated through completed transactions but currently
 2   withheld by Apple.
 3
           2.       Ex-Human develops consumer-facing artificial intelligence applications. Its
 4
     products, Botify AI (“Botify”) and Photify AI (“Photify”), have attracted large and engaged user
 5
     bases through Apple’s App Store. Botify, launched in August 2021, has generated more than 2.3
 6

 7   million iOS installs and approximately $330,000 in monthly revenue. Photify, launched in February

 8   2024, generates approximately $100,000 in monthly revenue.

 9         3.       On January 24, 2026, Apple issued a “Pending Termination Notice,” asserting that
10
     Ex-Human’s developer account had been used for “dishonest or fraudulent activity” in violation of
11
     Section 3.2(f) of the Apple Developer Program License Agreement (“DPLA”). Apple
12
     simultaneously froze all earnings associated with Botify and Photify. Ex-Human submitted
13
     multiple appeals and a reinstatement petition. In response, Apple repeatedly cited Section 3.2(f) but
14

15   did not identify any specific act, transaction, or submission that purportedly violated that provision.

16   Apple terminated Ex-Human’s developer account on March 13, 2026.
17         4.       Throughout the appeals process, Ex-Human provided detailed information
18
     regarding its applications, including their technical architecture and moderation systems. Apple’s
19
     responses remained generalized and non-specific, referring to categories of potential misconduct
20
     without identifying the conduct at issue. Despite having access to transaction-level data and
21

22   platform activity, Apple did not identify any particular transactions, user activity, or application

23   behavior that formed the basis of its determination.

24         5.       Ex-Human also attempted to engage Apple through additional channels, including
25   Apple’s App Store Business Management team, which had previously identified Ex-Human as a
26
     high-growth developer. Requests for direct communication with Apple’s App Review team were
27
     denied.
28
                                                   2
                                               COMPLAINT
        Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD          Document 1         Filed 03/31/26      Page 3 of 26



 1          6.       As a result of Apple’s actions, Ex-Human has been removed from the iOS platform,
 2   cutting off its ability to distribute its applications, maintain user relationships, and continue ongoing
 3
     subscription-based services. These harms are ongoing and cannot be fully remedied through
 4
     monetary damages alone.
 5
            7.       Apple has also continued to withhold approximately $500,000 in revenue generated
 6

 7   through completed transactions on Botify and Photify. Apple has not identified any specific

 8   transactions as fraudulent, subject to chargeback, or otherwise ineligible for payment, nor has it

 9   provided any accounting explaining the basis for withholding these funds.
10
            8.       Photify operates in a category of applications that overlaps in functionality with
11
     Apple’s own Image Playground offering, including user-generated image creation from selfies,
12
     style transformation, and avatar-based features. Apple removed Photify from the App Store while
13
     continuing to offer its own competing product on the same platform. In the absence of any identified
14

15   violation by Ex-Human, this context underscores the opacity of Apple’s decision-making process

16   and the absence of any articulated basis for its actions.
17          9.       Ex-Human brings this action for breach of contract, breach of the implied covenant
18
     of good faith and fair dealing, declaratory relief, unjust enrichment, and violations of California’s
19
     Unfair Competition Law. Ex-Human seeks injunctive relief restoring its Apple Developer Program
20
     membership, restoring Botify and Photify to availability on the App Store, and requiring Apple to
21

22   release withheld developer proceeds, as well as such other relief as the Court deems appropriate.

23                                              PARTIES
24          10.      Plaintiff Ex-Human is a Delaware corporation, with its principal place of business

25   in Boulder, Colorado.
26          11.      Defendant Apple is a California corporation formed and doing business under the
27
     laws of the state of California, with its principal place of business in Cupertino, California.
28
                                                    3
                                                COMPLAINT
           Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD       Document 1       Filed 03/31/26      Page 4 of 26



 1                                   JURISDICTION AND VENUE
             12.     This Court has subject matter jurisdiction over this action pursuant to 28 U.S.C.
 2

 3   § 1332 because the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000.00, exclusive of interest, costs, and

 4   attorneys’ fees, and because there is complete diversity between the parties, as this is an action

 5   between citizens of different states. Plaintiff Ex-Human is a citizen of Delaware and Colorado, and
 6
     Defendant Apple is a citizen of California.
 7
             13.     Apple is subject to personal jurisdiction in this Court pursuant to California Code of
 8
     Civil Procedure Section 410.10 because Apple is a citizen of or domiciled in California, operates
 9
     from its principal place of business in California, maintains substantial or continuous and systemic
10

11   contacts with California, has purposefully availed itself of the economic benefits of transacting

12   business in California, and has committed the tortious acts alleged in this Complaint in California.
13           14.     Venue in this Court is proper pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391 because Apple is located
14
     in this District and a substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to Ex-Human’s claims
15
     occurred in this District.
16
             15.     For the same reasons mentioned in the paragraphs above, the Divisional Assignment
17

18   is also proper pursuant to Local Rule 3-5(b).

19                                                   FACTS
20   I.       Apple’s App Store and Developer Program
21           16.    Apple designs, manufactures, and sells iPhones, which operate on Apple’s

22   proprietary mobile operating system, iOS.
23           17.     A mobile operating system (“OS”) is software that enables a smartphone’s core
24
     functions and allows users to run applications (“apps”) on the device. Applications must be
25
     developed for iOS in order to function on an iPhone.
26
             18.     iPhone users rely on both Apple-developed and third-party applications to fully
27

28   enjoy the capabilities of their devices.

                                                    4
                                                COMPLAINT
        Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD        Document 1       Filed 03/31/26     Page 5 of 26



 1         19.     Third-party developers, including Plaintiff Ex-Human, distribute iOS applications
 2   to iPhone users through Apple’s App Store. Apple owns and operates the App Store and administers
 3
     the processes through which applications are submitted, reviewed, and made available to iOS users.
 4

 5   II.    The Apple Developer Program License Agreement
           20.    Apple operates the App Store as the primary distribution channel for native iOS
 6
     applications on iPhone. Apple controls access to that distribution channel through its developer
 7

 8   program and app review processes, which are governed by the Apple Developer Program License

 9   Agreement (the “DPLA”).

10         21.     Apple drafts and imposes the DPLA as a condition of participation in the Apple
11
     Developer Program. Third-party developers, including Ex-Human, must assent to the DPLA in
12
     order to access Apple’s development tools, submit applications for review, and distribute
13
     applications through the App Store. The DPLA grants developers a limited, non-exclusive license
14
     to use Apple’s software, services, and distribution platform, subject to compliance with Apple’s
15

16   policies, App Review Guidelines, and related program requirements.

17         22.     To make an iOS application available on the App Store, a developer must submit
18   the application to Apple for review. Apple evaluates submitted applications through its review
19
     process and determines whether an application satisfies the DPLA and App Review Guidelines.
20
     Only applications that Apple approves may be distributed through the App Store.
21
           23.     The DPLA provides Apple with broad authority over the continued availability of
22

23   applications and developer accounts. Among other provisions, Apple reserves the right to suspend,

24   remove, or disable access to applications or developer accounts and to limit or revoke access to

25   Apple services in its discretion, including in circumstances where Apple believes that a developer
26   has violated applicable requirements.
27
           24.     The parties’ relationship with respect to paid applications and in-app purchases is
28
                                                 5
                                             COMPLAINT
       Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD          Document 1        Filed 03/31/26     Page 6 of 26



 1   governed by Schedule 2 to the DPLA, which Ex-Human entered into in order to distribute paid
 2   content and process App Store transactions. Under Schedule 2, Apple acts as the developer’s agent
 3
     and commissionaire for purposes of collecting and remitting payments from end users. Apple
 4
     collects payments on behalf of the developer and is responsible for processing those transactions
 5
     through its payment infrastructure.
 6

 7         25.      Section 2.8 of the DPLA provides that Apple “reserves the right to change, suspend,

 8   deprecate, deny, limit, or disable access to the Apple Services, or any part thereof, at any time

 9   without notice,” and that Apple “may revoke [a developer’s] access to the Apple Services, or may
10
     cancel the Apple Services (or any part thereof) at any time without notice or liability … in its sole
11
     discretion.”
12
           26.      Section 3.2(f) of the DPLA provides that developers may not engage in conduct that
13
     is unlawful, misleading, fraudulent, improper, or dishonest in connection with their applications or
14

15   the App Store, including conduct that interferes with Apple’s services or business practices. Apple

16   relied on Section 3.2(f) as the stated basis for its actions against Ex-Human.
17         27.      Although the DPLA provides Apple with discretion in administering its platform
18
     and enforcing its policies, Schedule 2 separately governs Apple’s role in collecting and remitting
19
     developer proceeds. Schedule 2 Section 7.1 permits Apple, upon termination, to withhold payments
20
     for a period reasonably necessary to calculate and offset End-User refunds, and also permits
21

22   withholding where Apple determines or suspects that a developer has engaged in suspicious,

23   misleading, fraudulent, improper, unlawful, or dishonest conduct.

24         28.      Schedule 2 does not provide that Apple may indefinitely retain all developer
25   proceeds from completed transactions without identifying any corresponding refunds, offsets, or
26
     transaction-specific basis for withholding. Nor does it describe a mechanism by which Apple may
27
     permanently retain earned developer revenue without accounting for how those funds are applied.
28
                                                  6
                                              COMPLAINT
        Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD         Document 1        Filed 03/31/26       Page 7 of 26



 1          29.     Ex-Human entered into the DPLA and Schedule 2 in order to develop and distribute
 2   its applications through the App Store and to process end-user transactions through Apple’s
 3
     payment system. In reliance on that relationship, Ex-Human built, operated, and maintained its
 4
     applications on Apple’s platform and routed all iOS transactions for Botify and Photify through
 5
     Apple’s payment infrastructure.
 6

 7   III.    Ex-Human Inc.
 8          30.   Ex-Human is a technology company that develops consumer-facing artificial

 9   intelligence applications. It was founded by Artem Rodichev, who previously served as Head of AI

10   at Replika, an AI companion platform used by millions of users worldwide.
11
            31.     Ex-Human created its Apple Developer Program account on April 26, 2021.
12
     Through this account, Ex-Human has distributed two applications on the App Store: Botify and
13
     Photify.
14
            32.     Ex-Human distributes these applications and provides ongoing updates and services
15

16   to users through Apple’s App Store. Ex-Human’s ability to reach iOS users, maintain existing

17   subscriptions, and operate these applications depends on continued access to the App Store and Ex-
18   Human’s Apple Developer Program membership.
19
            33.     Botify is an AI companion application that enables users to create and interact with
20
     AI-powered personas through natural conversation. Botify relies on Ex-Human’s application and
21
     model-serving infrastructure to deliver these features to end users.
22

23          34.     Botify had been continuously available on the App Store since August 30, 2021,

24   nearly four years at the time of the events giving rise to this action. Botify has accumulated more

25   than 2.3 million iOS installs and generates approximately $330,000 in monthly revenue.
26          35.     Photify is an AI image-generation application that enables users to generate and
27
     modify images and short-form video content using generative AI based on user-provided inputs,
28
                                                  7
                                              COMPLAINT
       Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD          Document 1         Filed 03/31/26   Page 8 of 26



 1   including text prompts and, in certain workflows, user-provided photos. Photify was launched on
 2   the App Store on February 23, 2024 and generates approximately $100,000 in monthly revenue.
 3
           36.      Both Botify and Photify are also available on the Google Play Store, where they
 4
     have remained continuously available and subject to Google’s independent review and compliance
 5
     processes. Google has taken no adverse action against either application, and both continue to
 6

 7   operate on Google Play without restriction.

 8
     IV.    Apple’s Image Playground: A Direct Competitor to Photify AI
 9         37.    Image Playground is an AI image-generation application developed, owned, and

10   distributed by Apple. Apple makes Image Playground available to iOS users through its platform.
11
           38.      Photify and Image Playground operate in the same category of consumer-facing AI
12
     image-generation applications and share overlapping functionality and user experience. Both
13
     applications enable users to generate images from user-provided inputs, including selfies; allow
14
     users to select among multiple faces or personas; offer a range of visual styles; and include user-
15

16   facing features for modifying appearance, such as virtual clothing or accessory transformations.

17         39.      Side-by-side comparisons of Photify and Image Playground reflect substantial
18   overlap in core user-facing functionality, including selfie-based image generation, multi-face
19
     selection, visual-style selection, and appearance modification features. Representative screenshots
20
     illustrating these similarities are shown below.

 1         40.      Apple removed Photify from the App Store while continuing to offer Image
 2   Playground on the same platform. As a result, Photify is no longer available to iOS users, while
 3
     Image Playground remains accessible through Apple’s distribution channel.
 4
           41.      Apple occupies a dual role within the iOS ecosystem relevant to this action. Apple
 5
     both controls access to iOS application distribution through the App Store and offers its own
 6

 7   applications within the same categories as third-party developers. In light of the substantial overlap

 8   between Photify and Image Playground, and the absence of any identified specific violation by Ex-

 9   Human, this context underscores the opacity of Apple’s decision-making process and supports Ex-
10
     Human’s request for discovery into the basis for Apple’s actions.
11
     V.     Apple’s Termination Notice and Ex-Human’s Appeals
12
           42.    On January 24, 2026, Apple sent Ex-Human a Pending Termination Notice through
13
     Photify’s App Store Connect messages, citing DPLA Section 3.2(f) and asserting that Ex-Human’s
14
     developer account “has been used for dishonest or fraudulent activity.” Apple simultaneously
15

16   paused all earnings payments to Ex-Human and removed Photify from the App Store, while Botify

17   remained available. The notice further stated that “[a]pp submissions from your account have
18   repeatedly violated the App Review Guidelines in an attempt to evade the review process” and that,
19
     “after multiple resubmissions, the guideline violation(s) detailed to you in prior correspondence
20
     remain unresolved.”
21
           43.      Apple’s January 24 notice did not identify the specific submission, transaction, act,
22

23   or guideline violation on which its determination was based. Nor did it identify the “prior

24   correspondence” to which it referred or explain what conduct Apple contended remained

25   unresolved.
26         44.      On January 25, 2026, Rodichev submitted an appeal on Ex-Human’s behalf to the
27
     App Review Board. The appeal provided Apple with a detailed explanation of Ex-Human’s
28
                                                 11
                                              COMPLAINT
       Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD         Document 1       Filed 03/31/26      Page 12 of 26



 1   technical architecture and content-moderation systems and offered to implement any additional
 2   measures Apple required.
 3
            45.      On February 10, 2026, Apple denied the appeal. Apple stated that “the
 4
     improvements you described in your appeal are insufficient to resolve the issues we previously
 5
     identified” and that it had found a “pattern of manipulative or misleading behavior.” Apple then
 6

 7   listed a non-exhaustive set of possible violations, including inaccurate metadata, misleading app

 8   content, inauthentic ratings manipulation, misleading customer support responses, and bait-and-

 9   switch purchasing practices. Apple did not state which, if any, of those categories it attributed to
10
     Ex-Human, and it did not identify any specific submission, transaction, or act.
11
            46.      On February 11, 2026, Rodichev submitted a reinstatement petition on Ex-Human’s
12
     behalf. The petition emphasized that Botify had remained continuously available on the App Store
13
     for nearly four years and had served more than one million iOS users, and that termination of Ex-
14

15   Human’s developer account would remove Botify even though Apple’s first three termination-

16   related communications had been directed to Photify.
17          47.      On February 20, 2026, Apple denied the reinstatement petition. The denial was
18
     substantively identical to Apple’s February 10 response: it again quoted Section 3.2(f), again
19
     referred generally to “manipulative or misleading behavior,” and again listed categories of possible
20
     misconduct without identifying the conduct Apple contended Ex-Human had engaged in. Apple
21

22   did not address Ex-Human’s arguments regarding Botify or identify any specific submission,

23   transaction, or act.

24          48.      On February 23, 2026, Apple sent a further communication that, for the first time,
25   identified specific App Review Guidelines: Guideline 1.1, Guideline 1.1.4, and Guideline 5.6.
26
     Apple stated that both Photify and Botify had been “rejected multiple times” for violations of those
27
     guidelines and characterized the violations as “egregious and repeated.” Even then, Apple did not
28
                                                 12
                                              COMPLAINT
       Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD          Document 1        Filed 03/31/26      Page 13 of 26



 1   identify the particular submissions, content, transactions, or acts underlying those characterizations.
 2         49.      On February 25, 2026, Rodichev submitted a third appeal on Ex-Human’s behalf.
 3
     In that appeal, Ex-Human narrowed its request and stated that it was not contesting Photify’s
 4
     removal. Ex-Human requested only that its Apple Developer Program membership be reinstated so
 5
     that Botify could remain available to its iOS user base.
 6

 7         50.      On February 27, 2026, Apple denied Ex-Human’s third appeal. Apple’s response

 8   repeated the same Section 3.2(f) language, the same cited App Review Guidelines, and the same

 9   generalized characterizations of “manipulative or misleading behavior” and “egregious and
10
     repeated” violations. Apple again did not identify any specific submission, transaction, or act, did
11
     not address Ex-Human’s narrowed request as to Botify, and did not identify any contractual basis
12
     for retaining Ex-Human’s withheld funds.
13
           51.      Separately, on February 26, 2026, Apple’s App Store Business Management team
14

15   contacted Ex-Human and identified it as part of a select group of developers with notable growth

16   on the App Store. During a March 4, 2026 call, Rodichev raised the pending termination. Apple’s
17   representative responded only that the App Review team “operates independently from Business
18
     Management” and that he could not influence review decisions.
19
           52.      On March 6, 2026, Rodichev submitted a fourth appeal on Ex-Human’s behalf. In
20
     that appeal, Ex-Human stated that it had implemented additional safeguards to strengthen
21

22   moderation, safety, and compliance across its apps. Ex-Human also explained that Botify AI serves

23   a large global user base and that termination of its developer account would disrupt access for many

24   users. Ex-Human reiterated its willingness to work with Apple.
25         53.      Apple’s Business Management team also provided a link through which Rodichev
26
     attempted to schedule a call directly with the App Review team. Rodichev made four separate
27
     attempts to do so, but each request was rejected. On March 10, 2026, Apple issued another denial
28
                                                  13
                                               COMPLAINT
       Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD          Document 1       Filed 03/31/26      Page 14 of 26



 1   that again cited Section 3.2(f) and the same App Review Guidelines, while still identifying no
 2   specific submission, transaction, or act.
 3
           54.      On March 13, 2026, Apple formally terminated Ex-Human’s Apple Developer
 4
     Program membership. The termination notice repeated the same Section 3.2(f)-based rationale
 5
     without identifying any new or specific factual basis. As an immediate consequence of the
 6

 7   termination, Botify was removed from the App Store, iOS in-app payment processing ceased, and

 8   Ex-Human lost access to Botify’s iOS user base.

 9
     VI.    Ex-Human’s Withheld Revenue
10         55.   Apple paused all earnings payments to Ex-Human effective January 24, 2026. As of
11
     the filing of this Complaint, Apple has withheld approximately $500,000 in developer revenue
12
     associated with completed App Store transactions across Botify and Photify.
13
           56.      These funds were generated through end-user purchases processed through Apple’s
14
     in-app payment system and collected by Apple in its role as Ex-Human’s agent and commissionaire
15

16   under Schedule 2 of the DPLA.

17         57.      Apple has access to transaction-level data for Botify and Photify, including
18   information sufficient to identify refunds, chargebacks, disputed transactions, and other
19
     transaction-specific adjustments. Apple has not identified any specific transaction that it contends
20
     is fraudulent, invalid, subject to chargeback, or otherwise ineligible for payment.
21
           58.      Apple has not provided Ex-Human with any accounting of the withheld funds,
22

23   including any breakdown identifying what portion of the withheld revenue, if any, corresponds to

24   refunds, offsets, or other transaction-specific adjustments.

25         59.      Based on Ex-Human’s historical data, Botify’s refund rate is approximately 1.5%
26   and Photify’s refund rate is approximately 1.0%. Apple has long had access to the data necessary
27
     to calculate any refund-related offsets or other payment adjustments. Any such offsets would
28
                                                    14
                                                 COMPLAINT
       Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD          Document 1        Filed 03/31/26      Page 15 of 26



 1   represent only a fraction of the approximately $500,000 currently withheld.
 2          60.     Schedule 2 Section 7.1 permits Apple, upon termination, to withhold payments for
 3
     a period reasonably necessary to calculate and offset End-User refunds and also permits
 4
     withholding where Apple determines or suspects that a developer has engaged in suspicious,
 5
     misleading, fraudulent, improper, unlawful, or dishonest conduct. Apple has not identified any
 6

 7   specific transactions, refunds, or conduct to which the withheld funds are tied, nor has it represented

 8   that the withheld funds have been applied to any such purpose.

 9          61.     Apple has not explained the basis on which it continues to retain 100% of Ex-
10
     Human’s earned revenue from completed transactions. Apple’s ongoing retention of those funds,
11
     without any identified transaction-level basis or accounting, is not tied to any disclosed refund
12
     obligation, offset, or other specific adjustment under the governing agreements.
13
            62.     Under Schedule 2, Apple collects end-user payments on behalf of developers and is
14

15   responsible for remitting those proceeds, subject to applicable offsets. Apple’s continued retention

16   of Ex-Human’s funds without providing any accounting or identified basis for withholding is
17   inconsistent with its role in collecting and remitting those proceeds.
18
     VII.    Harm to Ex-Human
19
            63.    Apple’s removal of Photify from the App Store has caused and continues to cause
20
     substantial harm to Ex-Human. Before its removal, Photify generated approximately $100,000 in
21
     monthly revenue through the App Store. Its removal eliminated Ex-Human’s ability to distribute
22

23   Photify to iOS users, continue serving existing iOS users through the App Store, and maintain the

24   application’s presence on the iOS platform.

25          64.     Botify was removed from the App Store on March 13, 2026, upon the formal
26   termination of Ex-Human’s developer account. Botify’s removal severed Ex-Human’s access to its
27
     iOS user base, disrupted Ex-Human’s ongoing subscription-based relationship with those users,
28
                                                  15
                                               COMPLAINT
       Case 3:26-cv-02798-JD           Document 1     Filed 03/31/26      Page 16 of 26



 1   and eliminated Botify’s primary revenue stream of approximately $330,000 per month. iOS in-app
 2   payment processing for Botify ceased upon termination.
 3
           65.      Apple’s continued withholding of approximately $500,000 in earned revenue causes
 4
     ongoing harm to Ex-Human independent of the application removals. Those withheld funds are
 5
     revenue generated through completed App Store transactions and are funds Ex-Human would
 6
